sources.summary: Korea Times (22 July 2024): the Seoul Central District Court ruled that a police officer's advice to an LGBTQ+ individual midway through legal gender change to "avoid using public restrooms for a while" infringed their personal rights; 300,000 won of a 3 million won claim awarded, final 2 July. Both first and second instances ruled for the plaintiff; the appellate court called comfortable restroom use "a fundamental and universal human right", and the officer received National Human Rights Commission human-rights education. Also cites the Commission's 2021 survey of 591 trans respondents (41% had used a restroom of a different gender than their identity out of fear; 39% avoided food and drinks; 36% forwent restroom use) and a 2021 Pohang branch ruling awarding 7 million won against an academy operator who barred a trans student from using restrooms.

NOTE: page body did not load at fetch time (navigation chrome only); the underlying Yonhap article (8 May 2024, tagged "legal sex change" / "transgender surgery") headlines a court ruling against mandating transgender surgery to change legal sex status — the national framework barring surgical requirements for legal gender recognition.

Hankyoreh (21 March 2024): youth LGBTQ+ organisation Dding Dong presented research on school safety for trans students (survey of 86 trans/genderqueer students, 24 Sept-7 Oct 2023): 59 of 86 (69%) felt uncomfortable using school restrooms, with respondents describing avoiding drinking water, waiting for empty stalls and leaving early; proposes amendments to the educational-facilities safety act, school health act and school-violence prevention act for inclusive facilities. Also covers a Busan-area study (January 2024, 208 LGBTQ students surveyed): 39% reported mistreatment such as outing, insults and violence at school because of gender identity or sexual orientation.
